+# Stochastic Interpolants with Data-Dependent Couplings — reproduction
+
+Reproduction of
+
+> M. S. Albergo\*, M. Goldstein\*, N. M. Boffi, R. Ranganath, E. Vanden-Eijnden,
+> **Stochastic Interpolants with Data-Dependent Couplings**, ICML 2024.
+
+The paper generalises the stochastic-interpolant framework so that the base
+density is *coupled* to the target: instead of `rho_0(x_0) rho_1(x_1)` one
+uses `rho_1(x_1) rho_0(x_0 | x_1)`.  The resulting interpolant
+`I_t = alpha_t x_0 + beta_t x_1 + gamma_t z` still has a velocity/score that
+are the minimisers of simple quadratic objectives, and the couplings make the
+transport cheaper and enable conditional generation tasks (in-painting,
+super-resolution) that do not need inference-time corrections.
+
+This repository implements
+
+1. **the framework and its theory** — Definition 3.1 / A.1, Theorem 3.1 / A.1
+   (transport equation, `L_b` and `L_g` objectives, score identity),
+   Corollary 3.1 / A.1 (probability-flow ODE and the forward/backward SDEs) and
+   Proposition 3.1 (transport-cost bound);
+2. **the couplings** — the independent baseline, the generic
+   `x_0 = m(x_1) + sigma zeta` construction of Section 3.2, the
+   data-decorruption coupling of Section 3.3, the in-painting coupling of
+   Section 4.1 and the super-resolution coupling of Section 4.2, including
+   conditioning on class labels and on image-shaped information `xi`;
+3. **the experiments** — Algorithm 1 (training), Algorithm 2 (sampling), the
+   DDPM U-Net of Appendix B with the exact hyper-parameters of the paper, the
+   ImageNet data pipeline (HuggingFace), the FID-50k evaluation of Tables 2/3
+   and the figure-generation utilities for Figures 1-6;
+4. **numerical verification of the theory** that runs on CPU in minutes —
+   Figure 2 (couplings vs conditioning on 3-mode Gaussian mixtures), the
+   transport-cost comparison of Section 3.3 / eq. (21) and Proposition 3.1,
+   plus a suite of unit tests that check every theoretical identity
+   numerically.
+
+Everything that does not require ImageNet-scale compute has been *run*; the
+ImageNet runs are fully implemented but are meant to be executed on GPUs
+(`200,000` gradient steps at batch size `32` per model, as specified in the
+addendum).
+
+---
+
+## 1. Results obtained in this reproduction
+
+### 1.1 Figure 2 — coupling is not the same as conditioning
+
+`experiments/gmm_coupling.py` (run: `bash scripts/run_toy_experiments.sh`)
+trains three velocity fields on two 3-mode Gaussian mixtures (a rotation+scale
+map `A` between the base and the target, base noise `sigma = 0.15`) and
+reports the transport-cost bound of Proposition 3.1, the realised transport
+cost of the learned ODE and the number of modes of the intermediate marginal
+`rho_{t=1/2}` (local maxima of a KDE):
+
+| setting | `int E|I_dot|^2 dt` (bound) | realised `E|X_1 - x_0|^2` | modes of `rho_{t=1/2}` |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| data-dependent coupling, unconditional `b_t(x)` | **1.321** | 1.288 | **3** |
+| conditioned `b_t(x, xi)` (independent within class) | 1.312 | 1.247 | 3 |
+| independent coupling, unconditional `b_t(x)` | 2.556 | 0.806 | **7** |
+
+The coupled transport keeps exactly the three modes of the problem while the
+uncoupled transport develops auxiliary modes (up to `3 x 3 = 9` are possible;
+7 are resolved here) — this is the qualitative statement of Figure 2.  Note
+that the realised cost can be lower than the bound for a *learned* model even
+in the uncoupled case (0.806 <= 2.556); what the coupling controls is the
+bound (Section 3.3), i.e. the complexity/cost of the underlying transport, and
+that is what the first and last columns show.
+
+![Figure 2 reproduction](results/gmm_figure2.png)
+
+### 1.2 Section 3.3 and Proposition 3.1 — coupling lowers the transport cost
+
+`experiments/transport_cost.py` (`bash scripts/run_toy_experiments.sh`):
+
+**(a) Equation (21)**, data-decorruption coupling `x_0 = x_1 + sigma zeta`
+(`sigma = 0.5`, `d` = dimension), coupled vs. independent with the same base
+marginal:
+
+| `d` | coupled (Monte Carlo) | `d sigma^2` | independent (Monte Carlo) | `2 E|x_1|^2 + d sigma^2` |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 2 | 0.502 | 0.500 | 4.528 | 4.535 |
+| 8 | 1.997 | 2.000 | 17.991 | 18.010 |
+| 64 | 16.015 | 16.000 | 143.935 | 143.990 |
+| 256 | 64.05 | 64.000 | 576.06 | 576.00 |
+
+**(b) Proposition 3.1** with the *exact* affine velocity of a Gaussian
+coupling (so the probability-flow ODE is integrated to high accuracy):
+
+| setting | `E|X_1(x_0) - x_0|^2` | bound `int E|I_dot|^2 dt` | inequality | `Var(X_1)` (target 1.0) |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `d=2`, coupled | 0.0283 | 0.5003 | holds | 1.012 |
+| `d=2`, independent | 0.0290 | 4.4654 | holds | 1.009 |
+| `d=8`, coupled | 0.1109 | 1.9996 | holds | 0.993 |
+| `d=8`, independent | 0.1149 | 18.019 | holds | 1.000 |
+| `d=2`, coupled, *learned* velocity net | 0.0293 | 0.5033 | holds | 1.004 |
+| `d=2`, independent, *learned* velocity net | 0.0636 | 4.4871 | holds | 0.905 |
+
+The exact-velocity rows also confirm that the flow recovers the target
+marginal (`Var(X_1) = 1`), i.e. the learned/analytic velocity really does
+transport the coupled base onto the target.
+
+### 1.3 Section 4.1 — in-painting pipeline (small-scale demonstration)
+
+`experiments/inpainting_demo.py` runs the *exact* procedure of Section 4.1
+(U-Net velocity model, 64-tile mask with `p = 0.3`, `x_0 = xi o x_1 + (1-xi) o
+zeta`, output masked to the missing region, `L_b` regression, ODE sampling)
+on a small procedural image dataset, and compares the data-dependent coupling
+with the independent (Gaussian base) baseline used in Table 2:
+
+| model | masked-region MSE | masked-region PSNR | max error on observed pixels |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| dependent coupling (ours) | see `results/inpainting_demo.json` | | ~0 (exact by construction) |
+| uncoupled baseline | see `results/inpainting_demo.json` | | large (nothing pins the observed pixels) |
+
+![in-painting demo, coupled](results/inpainting_demo_ours.png)
+
+The point of the comparison is the *structure* rather than the absolute
+numbers of the small CPU demonstration: with the coupling, the observed pixels
+are reproduced exactly for free, the missing region is filled from a
+distribution, and nothing has to be replaced or projected at inference time.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Repository layout
+
+```
+si_couplings/
+  interpolants.py   Definition 3.1 / A.1: schedules alpha, beta, gamma, the
+                    process I_t, its velocity, the effective noise scale
+                    gamma_tilde = alpha_t * sigma, and closed-form Gaussian
+                    reference quantities (used by the tests and experiments)
+  couplings.py      Section 3.2/3.3 and Section 4: IndependentCoupling,
+                    GaussianAdaptedCoupling, DataDecorruptionCoupling,
+                    InpaintingCoupling (64-tile mask), SuperResolutionCoupling
+  losses.py         Theorem 3.1 / A.1: L_b (eq. 7/22), L_g, and
+                    transport_cost_upper_bound (Proposition 3.1)
+  solvers.py        Corollary 3.1: probability-flow ODE (self-contained
+                    dopri5 + Euler = Algorithm 2 + Heun + optional torchdiffeq)
+                    and the forward/backward SDEs
+  train.py          Algorithm 1 with the Appendix-B optimiser recipe
+                    (Adam 2e-4, StepLR 0.99/1000 steps, clip 10,000, EMA)
+  sample.py         Algorithm 2 and the task-specific samplers
+  fid.py            Tables 2/3: FID-50k with an Inception-V3 feature extractor
+  visualize.py      Figures 3-6: [base | sample | ground truth] panels and
+                    temporal slices
+  data/             ImageNet via HuggingFace (`trust_remote_code=True`),
+                    mask sampling, super-resolution operators, synthetic
+                    stand-in dataset for smoke tests
+  models/           Appendix-B DDPM U-Net (time + class + image-shaped
+                    conditioning, output masking) and 2-D toy networks
+configs/            one YAML per experiment: in-painting 256/512 (coupled and
+                    baseline), super-resolution 64->256 (coupled and
+                    baseline), 256->512, plus a CPU smoke configuration
+scripts/            thin wrappers around the CLIs (train / evaluate FID /
+                    toy experiments / smoke test)
+experiments/        gmm_coupling.py (Figure 2), transport_cost.py
+                    (Section 3.3 + Proposition 3.1), inpainting_demo.py,
+                    super_resolution_demo.py
+tests/              pytest suite verifying the theory and the pipeline
+docs/theory.md      statement-by-statement map from the paper to the code
+results/            outputs produced by the runs above (figures + JSON)
+```
+
+`docs/theory.md` is the detailed map: every definition, theorem, corollary and
+proposition of the paper is listed there together with the function that
+implements it, the experiment that exercises it and the test that checks it.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Reproducing the ImageNet experiments
+
+### 3.1 Data
+
+ImageNet is loaded through HuggingFace, as suggested in the addendum:
+
+```python
+from datasets import load_dataset
+dataset = load_dataset("imagenet-1k", trust_remote_code=True)
+```
+
+`si_couplings/data/imagenet.py` wraps this into a `torch.utils.data.Dataset`
+that returns `(image, label)` with the image in `[-1, 1]` (random-resized-crop
++ horizontal flip for training, resize + centre crop for validation), which is
+the range expected by the U-Net of Appendix B.
+
+### 3.2 Training (Algorithm 1)
+
+```bash
+# in-painting, ImageNet-256x256
+bash scripts/train_inpainting_256_coupled.sh     # Table 2, "Dependent Coupling (Ours)"
+bash scripts/train_inpainting_256_baseline.sh    # Table 2, "Uncoupled Interpolant (Baseline)"
+bash scripts/train_inpainting_512_coupled.sh     # Figure 3, bottom panel
+
+# super-resolution
+bash scripts/train_superres_64_256_coupled.sh    # Table 3, "Dependent Coupling (Ours)"
+bash scripts/train_superres_256_512_coupled.sh   # Figure 6
+```
+
+Each run uses the numbers stated in the addendum (batch size 32, 200,000
+gradient steps) and in Appendix B (Adam at learning rate `2e-4`, StepLR with
+`gamma = 0.99` every `N = 1000` steps, no weight decay, gradient-norm clipping
+at 10,000, U-Net with `dim = 256`, `dim_mults = (1, 1, 2, 3, 4)`, 8 GroupNorm
+groups in the ResNet blocks, learned sinusoidal time conditioning of dimension
+32, 4 attention heads of dimension 64, no random Fourier features, class-label
+embeddings).  Manifests are written to `runs/<name>/train.jsonl` and
+checkpoints (with EMA weights) to `runs/<name>/checkpoint_last.pt`.
+
+### 3.3 Sampling and evaluation
+
+```bash
+# samples / panels (Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, 6)
+python -m si_couplings.sample --config configs/inpainting_256_coupled.yaml \
+    --checkpoint runs/inpainting_256_coupled/checkpoint_last.pt \
+    --task inpainting --n 6 --out results/inpainting_samples.pt
+
+# FID-50k (Tables 2 and 3)
+bash scripts/evaluate_fid_inpainting.sh
+bash scripts/evaluate_fid_superres.sh
+```
+
+The FID implementation (`si_couplings/fid.py`) uses the standard 2048-d
+Inception-V3 pool features and the 50,000-sample protocol; reference ImageNet
+statistics are cached next to the output file.
+
+---
+
+## 4. Tests and small-scale runs
+
+```bash
+pip install -r requirements.txt
+python -m pytest tests -q                     # 30 tests, ~40 s on CPU
+bash scripts/smoke_test.sh                    # tests + a tiny train/sample run
+bash scripts/run_toy_experiments.sh           # Figure 2 + Section 3.3 + Prop. 3.1
+python experiments/inpainting_demo.py --steps 200 --out results
+```
+
+The test suite covers
+
+* the boundary conditions and shapes of Definition 3.1, the positivity
+  condition `alpha^2 + beta^2 + gamma^2 > 0` and the equivalence of the
+  schedule printed in Section 4.1 with a time reversal of the default one;
+* the structural property of the in-painting interpolant,
+  `xi o I_t = xi o x_1` for all `t` (hence `b_t = 0` on observed pixels), the
+  64-tile mask distribution and `E|x_0 - x_1|^2 = d sigma^2` for the
+  data-decorruption coupling;
+* Theorem 3.1: the marginal of `I_t`, the identity
+  `grad log rho_t = -gamma_t^{-1} g_t` (kernel-regression check),
+  `b_t = E[I_dot | I_t = .]` (least-squares check) and the equivalence of the
+  `L_b` objective with the MSE form;
+* Corollary 3.1: the forward SDE transports base to target and the backward
+  SDE transports target to base, and `eps_t = 0` reproduces the ODE;
+* Proposition 3.1: the inequality `E|X_1 - x_0|^2 <= int E|I_dot|^2 dt` and
+  recovery of the target marginal;
+* the solvers (dopri5 against an analytic solution) and an end-to-end
+  train/sample smoke test on synthetic images (in-painting and
+  super-resolution, coupled and uncoupled).
+
+---
+
+## 5. Deviations, assumptions and conventions
+
+* **`alpha_t`, `beta_t` for the in-painting experiment.**  Section 4.1 writes
+  "we set `alpha_t = t` and `beta_t = 1 - t`".  That pair is the time-reversed
+  labelling of the interpolant (it satisfies `alpha_1 = beta_0 = 1`, not the
+  `alpha_0 = beta_1 = 1` of Definition 3.1) and it contradicts Algorithm 2,
+  which initialises `X_0 = m(x_1) + sigma zeta` and integrates forward to the
+  clean image.  We follow Definition 3.1 / Algorithm 2 and use
+  `alpha_t = 1 - t`, `beta_t = t` everywhere; `LinearInterpolant(reverse=True)`
+  reproduces the literal statement if desired (the two are related by
+  `t -> 1 - t`, so the learned transport is the same).
* **`attn_resolutions`.**  Appendix B lists the number of attention heads and
  their dimension but not the resolutions at which full attention is inserted.
  We insert full attention at 16x16 and 32x32 (the innermost resolutions of the
  256x256 model, matching the reference implementation's behaviour of using
  full attention only at the lowest resolution) and linear attention at every
  resolution.
* **Base distribution for the uncoupled baseline.**  The baseline is the
  standard stochastic interpolant, `x_0 ~ N(0, Id)` independent of `x_1`, with
  `gamma_t = sqrt(2 t (1 - t))`; for the in-painting comparison the *same* mask
  is used for both models so that the two differ only in the coupling.
* **`sigma` of the couplings.**  The paper does not state a numerical value
  for the super-resolution / in-painting noise scale `sigma`.  We use
  `sigma = 0.5` (super-resolution) and `sigma = 1` on the missing tiles
  (in-painting, i.e. `zeta ~ N(0, Id)`, exactly as written in Section 4.1);
  `configs/*.yaml` exposes both.
* **FID.**  The paper reports FID-50k.  `si_couplings/fid.py` implements the
  Frechet distance with the usual Inception-V3 features (pool layer, images
  resized to 299x299 and normalised to `[-1, 1]`); the baseline FID numbers in
  Tables 2 and 3 are quoted from the paper (and the addendum explicitly puts
  the Improved DDPM / SR3 / ADM / Cascaded Diffusion / I^2SB baselines out of
  scope), so only our own two rows are reproduced here.
* **Compute.**  No GPU was available in the environment used to write this
+; the ImageNet runs are therefore implemented and unit/smoke-tested but not
+  executed.  Everything in Section 1 above was executed on CPU.
*** End Patch

Reproduction of

> M. S. Albergo\*, M. Goldstein\*, N. M. Boffi, R. Ranganath, E. Vanden-Eijnden,
> **Stochastic Interpolants with Data-Dependent Couplings**, ICML 2024.

The paper generalises the stochastic-interpolant framework so that the base
density is *coupled* to the target: instead of `rho_0(x_0) rho_1(x_1)` one
uses `rho_1(x_1) rho_0(x_0 | x_1)`.  The resulting interpolant
`I_t = alpha_t x_0 + beta_t x_1 + gamma_t z` still has a velocity and a score
that are the minimisers of simple quadratic objectives, and the couplings make
the transport cheaper and enable conditional generation tasks (in-painting,
super-resolution) that need no inference-time corrections.

1. **the framework and its theory** - Definition 3.1 / A.1, Theorem 3.1 / A.1
   (transport equation, `L_b` and `L_g` objectives, score identity),
   Corollary 3.1 / A.1 (probability-flow ODE and the forward/backward SDEs) and

```bash
bash scripts/run_toy_experiments.sh           # Figure 2 + Section 3.3 + Prop. 3.1
python experiments/inpainting_demo.py --steps 200 --out results
python experiments/super_resolution_demo.py --steps 200 --out results
```

The test suite covers

* the boundary conditions and shapes of Definition 3.1, the positivity
  condition `alpha^2 + beta^2 + gamma^2 > 0`, and the equivalence of the
  schedule printed in Section 4.1 with a time reversal of the default one;
* the structural property of the in-painting interpolant,
  `xi o I_t = xi o x_1` for all `t` (hence `b_t = 0` on the observed pixels),
  the 64-tile mask distribution, and `E|x_0 - x_1|^2 = d sigma^2` for the
  data-decorruption coupling;
* Theorem 3.1: the marginal of `I_t`, the identity
  `grad log rho_t = -gamma_t^{-1} g_t` (kernel-regression check),
  `b_t = E[I_dot | I_t = .]` (least-squares check), and the equivalence of the
  `L_b` objective with the MSE form;
* Corollary 3.1: the forward SDE transports base to target, the backward SDE
  transports target to base, and `eps_t = 0` reproduces the ODE;
* Proposition 3.1: the inequality `E|X_1 - x_0|^2 <= int E|I_dot|^2 dt` and
  recovery of the target marginal;
* the solvers (dopri5 against an analytic solution) and an end-to-end
  train/sample smoke test on synthetic images (in-painting and
  super-resolution, coupled and uncoupled).

---

## 5. Deviations, assumptions and conventions

* **`alpha_t`, `beta_t` for the in-painting experiment.**  Section 4.1 writes
  "we set `alpha_t = t` and `beta_t = 1 - t`".  That pair is the time-reversed
  labelling of the interpolant (it satisfies `alpha_1 = beta_0 = 1`, not the
  `alpha_0 = beta_1 = 1` of Definition 3.1) and it contradicts Algorithm 2,
  which initialises `X_0 = m(x_1) + sigma zeta` and integrates forward to the
  clean image.  We follow Definition 3.1 and Algorithm 2 and use
  `alpha_t = 1 - t`, `beta_t = t` everywhere; `LinearInterpolant(reverse=True)`
  reproduces the literal statement (the two differ by `t -> 1 - t`, so the
  learned transport is the same).
* **`attn_resolutions`.**  Appendix B lists the number of attention heads and
  their dimension, but not the resolutions at which full attention is
  inserted.  We insert full attention at the innermost resolutions (16x16 and
  32x32 for 256x256 images, matching the reference implementation's behaviour
  of using full attention only at the lowest resolution) and linear attention
  at every resolution.
* **Base distribution of the uncoupled baseline.**  The baseline is the
  standard stochastic interpolant, `x_0 ~ N(0, Id)` independent of `x_1`, with
  `gamma_t = sqrt(2 t (1 - t))`; for the in-painting comparison the *same*
  mask is used for both models, so the two differ only in the coupling.
* **The noise scale `sigma` of the couplings.**  The paper does not state a
  numerical value for the super-resolution noise scale.  We use
  `sigma = 0.5` for super-resolution and `sigma = 1` on the missing tiles for
  in-painting (i.e. `zeta ~ N(0, Id)`, exactly as written in Section 4.1);
  both are exposed in `configs/*.yaml`.
* **FID.**  The paper reports FID-50k.  `si_couplings/fid.py` implements the
  Frechet distance with the usual Inception-V3 features (images resized to
  299x299, normalised from the `[-1, 1]` model range); the baseline rows of
  Tables 2 and 3 are quoted from the paper, and the addendum explicitly puts
  the Improved DDPM / SR3 / ADM / Cascaded Diffusion / I^2SB baselines out of
  scope, so only our own two rows are reproduced here.
* **Compute.**  No GPU was available in the environment in which this
  reproduction was written, so the ImageNet runs are implemented and covered
  by unit and smoke tests but were not executed; everything reported in
  Section 1 was executed on CPU and the raw outputs are in `results/`.

Two issues:
1. The triplet grid still fails: "Expected size 32 but got size 4". Hmm: rows are built as (C, H, W_total) — then `out` contains rows of shape (3, 32, W_total). The separator zeros(row.shape[0], gap, row.shape[2]) = (3, 4, W_total) — that matches. The error says tensor number 1 has size 32 vs expected 4 in dimension 1... Wait "Expected size 32 but got size 4" means dim 1 of tensor 1 is 4 while previous is 32. Tensor 1 is the separator with shape (3, 4, W_total)?? That means row.shape[0] = 3, gap = 4 → dim1 = 4; but the previous tensor (row) has dim1 = 32. So the separator needs to be (C, gap, W) — I set (row.shape[0], gap, row.shape[2]) = (3, 4, W) — that IS (C=3, gap=4, W). And the row is (3, 32, W). So dim 1: 4 vs 32 → mismatch! Because the separator's dim1 = gap = 4 ≠ H = 32. So the separator should be (C, gap, W) where the *height* of the separator is `gap` and it's placed *between rows* — that's right conceptually (a horizontal band of height `gap`). But then dimension 1 (height) is 4 for the separator and 32 for the rows — that's correct! You can't concatenate rows of different heights.

Right: cat along dim=0 requires all other dims equal. A separator band of height `gap` has a different height than the row — so concatenating gives different sizes in dim1, which is where the error came from... wait no: for `torch.cat(out, dim=0)`, all tensors must have the same shape except dim 0. A separator of shape (3, 4, W) has dim1=4 while rows have dim1=32 → error. Hmm! But the concatenation along dim 0 is on the height dimension, so a separator band must also have height 4 → it has shape (3, 4, W) and its dim1 IS the height = 4, but the rows have height 32. Since cat(dim=0) concatenates along the height, the OTHER dims must match: dim1 for a (3,4,W) separator is 4, and dim2 = W. Hmm — dim1 of the separator (4) is being treated as "height"?? No! For a tensor (C, H, W), dim0 = C, dim1 = H, dim2 = W. Concatenating along dim0 concatenates the CHANNEL dimension. Oops!

I need to concatenate along dim=1 (height) for rows and dim=2 (width) for the horizontal separators:

- Horizontal layout: `torch.cat([a, sep_v, b, sep_v, c], dim=2)` where sep_v has shape (C, H, gap) ✓ (that's what I do).
- Vertical stacking: `torch.cat(out, dim=1)` with separators of shape (C, gap, W_total) ✓.

Fix: `return torch.cat(out, dim=1)`.

2. For the SR task with the baseline independent coupling, `coupling.scale` doesn't exist. I need to handle the baseline: the low-res image should come from a separate scale parameter. Let me add to `config()` a top-level "superres_scale" and use it in evaluate; or better, in `evaluate`, use `getattr(coupling, "scale", 2)`. Also in `sample_super_resolution`, the coupling must be a SuperResolutionCoupling (it uses coupling.upsample); for the baseline we need a different path: for the baseline SR model, we still need the conditioning ξ (low-res upsampled) but the base x0 ~ N(0,I). So the baseline for SR should be: `sample_super_resolution` must handle a general coupling — base x0 from the coupling (N(0,I)) and the conditioning ξ = U(D(x_1)) which the model needs. For the independent coupling the model doesn't have cond channels... Hmm: for a fair SR baseline, the model should still receive the low-res conditioning (that's the standard conditional generation baseline: b_t(x, ξ) trained with an independent Gaussian base). So we'd need a hybrid: independent coupling but with conditioning ξ.

That's an important detail for a "fair" SR baseline. In the paper, Table 3 doesn't include an uncoupled SI baseline (only I²SB etc. which are out of scope). So the SR-baseline config is my addition. To be correct, the baseline should be: x0 ~ N(0,I), conditioning ξ = U(D(x1)) passed to the model (so the model can condition on the low-res image, which is essential for a reasonable SR baseline).

Implementation: add a `cond_fn` option to IndependentCoupling? Better: introduce a `ConditioningCoupling`-like wrapper: the generic design is that the coupling produces (x0, cond, mask). For the SR baseline I want x0 ~ N(0,I) and cond = U(D(x1)).

I'll add to IndependentCoupling an optional `cond_fn` that computes the conditioning from x1 (with `cond_channels` configurable). Then `SuperResolutionBaseline` = IndependentCoupling(cond_fn=lambda x1: paired_lowres(x1, scale), cond_channels=3). Hmm, IndependentCoupling is defined with `channels` etc.

Simplest: add to IndependentCoupling `__init__(base_scale, channels, image_size, cond_fn=None, cond_channels=0)`, and in sample_base return `cond = cond_fn(x1) if cond_fn else None`. Then in the config for SR baseline, I can't express cond_fn in YAML. So instead, let me add a dedicated class `SuperResolutionBaselineCoupling(SuperResolutionCoupling)` that overrides sample_base to use x0 ~ N(0,I) with cond = U(D(x1)). That's clean:

```python
class IndependentConditionedCoupling(Coupling):
    """Independent Gaussian base with an image-shaped conditioning signal."""
    def __init__(self, base_scale=1.0, cond_fn=None, cond_channels=0)
```

Let me implement `SuperResolutionBaselineCoupling`:
```python
class SuperResolutionBaselineCoupling(SuperResolutionCoupling):
    name = "super_resolution_baseline"
    self_noised = False
    def sample_base(self, x1, xi=None, **kw):
        xi = self.upsample(self.downsample(x1), size=x1.shape[-2:]) if xi is None else xi
        x0 = self.base_scale * torch.randn_like(x1)
        return x0, xi, None, 0.0
```
And for sampling: given low-res → ξ = U(low) and x0 ~ N(0,I) with cond=ξ. `sample_super_resolution` needs to branch on the coupling type: if it's a baseline coupling, x0 = randn * base_scale; else x0 = ξ + σζ.

Let me generalize `sample_super_resolution`: 
```python
if isinstance(coupling, SuperResolutionBaselineCoupling) -> x0 = coupling.base_scale*randn; cond = xi
else: x0 = xi + sigma*randn; cond=xi
```

 ```
Committed. Now, do I have time/need for more improvements? I'm at roughly 2h50m of the 3h budget. The instructions say to use the time available and continue refining.

High-value remaining items:
1. **Verify the FID pipeline end-to-end on a small scale** (`python -m si_couplings.fid --smoke`?) — the `--smoke` flag exists but isn't implemented as such (it's parsed but unused). Let me actually test the fid CLI with a tiny synthetic run: need a config + checkpoint with synthetic data, and compare against the synthetic dataset's "real" images. The fid CLI uses `build_dataloader(cfg, train=False, ...)` which for synthetic data returns the same SyntheticImages (n=... ) — FID between synthetic model samples and synthetic images. This validates the CLI path. It requires image_size ≥ ... Inception resizes to 299 anyway. Let me try with the smoke config: 32×32 images, n=50, batch 8, steps 10. And a checkpoint from /tmp/si_smoke? That checkpoint was trained on the smoke config (32×32, 4 classes). Let me run:

python3 -m si_couplings.fid --config configs/smoke_synthetic.yaml --checkpoint /tmp/si_smoke/checkpoint_last.pt --n 32 --batch-size 8 --steps 8 --method euler --out /tmp/fid_smoke.json

Note: `compute_statistics` with n_samples=32 and 2048-dim features → covariance matrix 2048² is fine but with 32 samples it's singular; sqrtm may produce complex/NaN → my code handles with offset. Let's see if it runs. This is a real validation of the FID code path (the most important metric in the paper). Let me do it.

Also note `fid.py`'s generated_batches for task "inpainting" calls sample_inpainting(model, coupling, images, ...) and yields the *whole-image* samples — the paper's FID for inpainting is computed on the completed images (full images), which is what we do ✓ (as x_t=1 is a full image; the observed pixels are the ground truth).

2. Add `scripts/run_all.sh` that runs everything in order (with a note that GPU is required).

3. Maybe add `si_couplings/evaluate.py` for PSNR/SSIM metrics? Not needed.

Let me do the FID smoke test now.

raw_content:
The FID pipeline runs end-to-end but the value is absurd because with n=32 samples the 2048×2048 covariance is singular and sqrtm blows up. That's expected for tiny n (FID-50k is the real protocol), but let me make the implementation more robust:
- Use a regularization: add eps·I to the covariances before sqrtm (standard practice, e.g., pytorch-fid uses eps=1e-6 but relies on n≫d).

"""FID utilities (Tables 2 and 3) - checked without downloading Inception."""

import torch

from si_couplings.fid import compute_statistics, frechet_distance


def test_frechet_distance_analytic_gaussians():
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    d = 8
    mu = torch.zeros(d, dtype=torch.float64)
    A = torch.randn(d, d, dtype=torch.float64)
    s1 = A @ A.T / d + torch.eye(d, dtype=torch.float64)
    B = torch.randn(d, d, dtype=torch.float64)
    s2 = B @ B.T / d + torch.eye(d, dtype=torch.float64)
    assert frechet_distance({"mu": mu, "sigma": s1}, {"mu": mu, "sigma": s1}) < 1e-8
    far = frechet_distance({"mu": mu, "sigma": s1}, {"mu": mu + 1.0, "sigma": s2})
    assert far > 0.5


def test_compute_statistics_recovers_moments():
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    d, n = 4, 20_000
    feats = torch.randn(n, d)

    def feature_fn(x):  # the "extractor" is the identity here
        return x

    stats = compute_statistics(feature_fn, [feats], n_samples=n)
    assert stats["n"] == n
    assert torch.allclose(stats["mu"].float(), feats.mean(0), atol=1e-5)
    assert torch.allclose(stats["sigma"].float(), torch.cov(feats.T), atol=1e-3)


def test_compute_statistics_respects_n_samples():
    feats = torch.randn(100, 3)
    stats = compute_statistics(lambda x: x, [feats], n_samples=10)
    assert stats["n"] == 10
 ```

The reproduction is complete and committed. Here's what's in the submission.

## What I built

A full implementation of *Stochastic Interpolants with Data-Dependent Couplings* (ICML 2024) at [/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission), organized along the paper:

- **Theory** — [interpolants.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/interpolants.py) (Definition 3.1/A.1, schedules, effective noise scale `γ̃_t = α_t σ`), [losses.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/losses.py) (the `L_b`/`L_g` objectives of Theorem 3.1), [solvers.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/solvers.py) (probability-flow ODE with a self-contained dopri5 + Euler = Algorithm 2, and the forward/backward SDEs of Corollary 3.1).
- **Couplings** — [couplings.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/couplings.py): independent baseline, generic `x₀ = m(x₁) + σζ`, data-decorruption, in-painting (`x₀ = ξ∘x₁ + (1−ξ)∘ζ`, 64 tiles, p=0.3) and super-resolution (`x₀ = U(D(x₁)) + σζ`), plus uncoupled-but-conditioned baselines.
- **Experiments** — Appendix-B DDPM U-Net (252M params, exact listed hyper-parameters, class + image-shaped conditioning, velocity output masking), Algorithm 1 training with the paper's optimiser recipe and the addendum's batch 32 / 200k steps, HuggingFace ImageNet loading, FID-50k, panel/figure utilities, one YAML per experiment, and shell scripts.

## What I actually ran here (CPU)

| Experiment | Result |
|---|---|
| Figure 2 (3-mode GMMs) | coupled 3 intermediate modes vs. independent 7; bound 1.32 vs. 2.56 |
| Eq. (21) | coupled = `dσ²` (0.502, 1.99, 16.0, 64.0 for d=2,8,64,256) vs. independent `2E‖x₁‖²+dσ²` |
| Prop. 3.1 | inequality verified with exact and learned velocities; target variance recovered (≈1.0) |
| In-painting demo | masked MSE 0.0346 / PSNR 20.6 and **0.0** error on observed pixels, vs. baseline 0.237 / 12.3 / 2.0 |
| Super-resolution demo | MSE 0.0144 / PSNR 24.4 vs. baseline 0.0866 / 16.6 |
| Tests | 34 pytest tests, all passing (verified after `git clone` + `git clean -fd`) |

Raw numbers and figures are in `results/`; the ImageNet runs are implemented and config-validated but not executed (no GPU), with `bash scripts/run_all.sh` as the entry point.

## Judgement calls worth flagging

Section 4.1 states `α_t = t, β_t = 1−t`, which is the time-reversed labelling and contradicts Definition 3.1 and Algorithm 2; I followed the definition/algorithm and documented the reversal (both are implemented). `attn_resolutions` isn't given in Appendix B so I chose the innermost resolutions. Both are recorded in the README along with the FID protocol and σ choices.

## What I built

A full implementation of *Stochastic Interpolants with Data-Dependent Couplings* (ICML 2024) at [/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission), organized along the paper:

- **Theory** — [interpolants.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/interpolants.py) (Definition 3.1/A.1, schedules, effective noise scale `γ̃_t = α_t σ`), [losses.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/losses.py) (the `L_b`/`L_g` objectives of Theorem 3.1), [solvers.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/solvers.py) (probability-flow ODE with a self-contained dopri5 + Euler = Algorithm 2, and the forward/backward SDEs of Corollary 3.1).
- **Couplings** — [couplings.py](/Users/apple/Documents/0919-test/codex/work/stochastic-interpolants-codex-desktop/submission/si_couplings/couplings.py): independent baseline, generic `x₀ = m(x₁) + σζ`, data-decorruption, in-painting (`x₀ = ξ∘x₁ + (1−ξ)∘ζ`, 64 tiles, p=0.3) and super-resolution (`x₀ = U(D(x₁)) + σζ`), plus uncoupled-but-conditioned baselines.
- **Experiments** — Appendix-B DDPM U-Net (252M params, exact listed hyper-parameters, class + image-shaped conditioning, velocity output masking), Algorithm 1 training with the paper's optimiser recipe and the addendum's batch 32 / 200k steps, HuggingFace ImageNet loading, FID-50k, panel/figure utilities, one YAML per experiment, and shell scripts.
